subject: maths

concepts.title: Irreducible Factors of Algebraic Expressions
concepts.definition: Representing a term from an algebraic expression as a product of basic components, including numbers and variables, which cannot be broken down any further.
concepts.key_idea: Decompose an algebraic term into its most fundamental, indivisible multipliers.
question_patterns: find the irreducible factors of {term}
what are the prime factors of the algebraic term {term}
express the term {term} in its irreducible form
write down the basic factors of {term}
determine the irreducible components of {term}

solution_steps.action: Find prime factors of the numerical coefficient
solution_steps.explain: Express the numerical coefficient of the term as a product of prime numbers.
Write each variable raised to a power as a repeated product of that variable.

solution_steps.action: Combine the numerical and variable factors
solution_steps.explain: Write the entire term as a product of all the prime numbers and individual variables.

concepts.title: Factorisation by Common Factors Method
concepts.definition: A method where we identify the highest common factor among all terms of an expression and extract it using the distributive property.
concepts.key_idea: Extract the greatest shared monomial factor from all terms of the polynomial.
question_patterns: factorise the expression {expr} using common factors
find the common factors and factorise {expr}
extract the common factor from {expr}
how do you factorise {expr} by taking out common terms
calculate the factored form of {expr} by finding common factors

solution_steps.action: Write each term in its irreducible factor form
solution_steps.explain: Break down every term of the expression into its prime numerical and variable factors.
Find the factors that are present in every single term of the expression.
Use the distributive law to write the common factors outside a bracket, leaving the remaining parts of each term inside.

concepts.title: Factorisation by Regrouping Terms
concepts.definition: Arranging terms into smaller groups that share common factors, allowing a common binomial factor to emerge across the entire expression.
concepts.formula: a*x + b*x + a*y + b*y = (a + b)*(x + y)
concepts.key_idea: Group terms in pairs to find a common binomial multiplier.
question_patterns: factorise the expression {expr} by regrouping its terms
regroup the terms of {expr} and find its factors
how to factorise {expr} using the regrouping method
obtain the factors of {expr} by grouping terms
use regrouping to factorise the polynomial {expr}

solution_steps.action: Group the terms of the expression
solution_steps.explain: Rearrange and group the terms into pairs or sets such that each group has a common factor.

solution_steps.action: Factor out common monomials from each group
solution_steps.explain: Extract the common factor from each individual group to reveal a common binomial factor.
Combine the terms by factoring out the shared binomial expression from both parts.

concepts.title: Factorisation using Perfect Square Identities
concepts.definition: Using standard algebraic identities for squared binomials to convert three-term quadratic expressions into perfect squares.
concepts.key_idea: Match trinomials to standard square expansions to write them as squared binomials.
question_patterns: factorise the perfect square trinomial {expr}

express the trinomial {expr} as a perfect square
find the factors of {expr} using standard algebraic identities

solution_steps.action: Identify the first and last terms as perfect squares
solution_steps.explain: Check if the first and third terms can be written as squares of some terms, say a^2 and b^2.
Check if the middle term is equal to 2*a*b or -2*a*b.
Write the expression as (a + b)^2 or (a - b)^2 depending on the sign of the middle term.

concepts.title: Factorisation using Difference of Squares Identity
concepts.definition: Factoring a binomial consisting of one square term subtracted from another into the product of their sum and difference.
concepts.key_idea: Rewrite a difference of two squares as a product of conjugate binomials.
question_patterns: factorise the binomial {expr} using the difference of squares

solution_steps.action: Express both terms as perfect squares
solution_steps.explain: Rewrite the binomial in the form a^2 - b^2.

solution_steps.action: Apply the difference of squares identity
solution_steps.explain: Use the formula a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)*(a + b) to factorise the expression.

concepts.title: Factorisation of Quadratic Trinomials
concepts.definition: Factoring quadratic trinomials by splitting the middle term into two parts whose coefficients multiply to the constant term and add to the linear coefficient.
concepts.key_idea: Find two numbers that multiply to the constant and add to the middle coefficient to split the middle term.
question_patterns: factorise the quadratic expression {expr} of the form x^2 + px + q

solution_steps.action: Find two numbers with the required sum and product
solution_steps.explain: Identify two numbers, a and b, such that their product ab equals the constant term q, and their sum a+b equals the coefficient p.
Rewrite the middle term px as ax + bx.
Group the terms as (x^2 + ax) + (bx + ab) and factor out the common terms to get (x + a)*(x + b).

concepts.title: Division of a Monomial by another Monomial
concepts.definition: Dividing a single-term algebraic expression by another by simplifying their numerical coefficients and subtracting exponents of common variables.
concepts.key_idea: Cancel out common numerical and variable factors from the numerator and denominator.

solution_steps.action: Write the division as a fraction
solution_steps.explain: Express the division with the first monomial in the numerator and the second in the denominator.

Cancel the common numbers and variables to find the simplified quotient.

concepts.title: Division of a Polynomial by a Monomial
concepts.definition: Dividing a multi-term algebraic expression by a single term by dividing each term of the polynomial individually.
concepts.formula: (A + B + C) / D = A/D + B/D + C/D
concepts.key_idea: Distribute the division by dividing every term of the polynomial by the divisor monomial.

solution_steps.explain: Split the fraction so that each individual term of the numerator is divided by the denominator monomial.

concepts.title: Division of a Polynomial by a Polynomial
concepts.definition: Dividing one multi-term expression by another by factorising both the dividend and divisor completely and cancelling common factors.
concepts.key_idea: Factorise both polynomials first, then cancel out any common binomial or polynomial factors.
